_about: What you can actually rent at each housing place: units (rent inside the tier's band, how many are free), quirks (perk, snag or odd) and the neighbors you'd live next to. Landlords and their terms are in data/landlords.json. Drafted by Claude for Eko; every name, unit and neighbor here is draft until Eko and Nib sign it off. A unit with staff is the crew rate for people who work there (honor system); a unit with pay is paid in something other than credits.

units.name: Seventh-floor room
units.blurb: The cheapest room in the building, because nobody wants to climb seven flights.

units.name: Third-floor flat
units.blurb: Two rooms, a window onto the street, and radiators that knock all night.

units.name: Home above a shop
units.blurb: Right over the street-level shops, so you get shop noise until ten.

quirks.text: The elevators have been "under assessment" for as long as anyone can remember, so plan on the stairs.
Fix an elevator and Halvard Mercy sends you a thank-you letter, followed by a rent hike for the improved unit.
There have been three owners since 1987, so three sets of keys still work and nobody checks who comes and goes.

neighbors.name: Dot Kessler
neighbors.who: Runs the second-floor laundry line and the building's group chat.
neighbors.hook: Knows who's behind on rent before the landlord does.

neighbors.name: Old Faro
neighbors.who: Has been "assessing" the east elevator himself for six years.
neighbors.hook: He's looking for a Wrench to help him finally finish it.

units.name: Upper-floor room
units.blurb: Fifth floor, on the far side of the U. Realistically, you'll be taking the stairs.

units.name: Courtyard flat
units.blurb: Looks onto the courtyard, so you hear everyone's business and they hear yours.

units.name: Corner unit over the Fryer
units.blurb: Warm all winter. It smells like the Fryer all year round.

quirks.text: Two elevators, and neither works often enough to rely on.
Ma Dresk's Fryer is downstairs, so there's always a hot meal on the walk home.
Ma Dresk always knows who's behind on rent, and so does the whole Fryer.

neighbors.name: Pip Arrowsmith
neighbors.who: Fourth floor. Sells hand-mended coats from the landing.
neighbors.hook: Will trade a coat for a story she hasn't heard.

neighbors.name: Brannoch
neighbors.who: Works night shifts on the docks and sleeps all day.
neighbors.hook: Will fight anyone who runs the stairs before noon.

units.name: Courtyard room
units.blurb: A single room off the courtyard, under one of the lamps.

units.name: Two-room family house
units.blurb: A small house with its own door and a private patch of courtyard.

units.name: The house with the lamp that won't go out
units.blurb: Cheaper than the rest. The lamp outside its door stays lit no matter what anyone does.

quirks.text: The courtyard lamps are never quite off.
Rent receipts arrive signed in handwriting that isn't hers.
Ember Court's occult trade is a two-minute walk away. Shades and Signals can get their supplies close to home.

neighbors.name: Mister Ashby
neighbors.who: Rents the house by the gate. Nobody has ever seen him pay rent.
neighbors.hook: Claims to have "an arrangement" and won't say with whom.

neighbors.name: Ruth Calloway
neighbors.who: The third tenant in Number 4 this year.
neighbors.hook: Wants to know what happened to the first two.

units.name: Room over the stall
units.blurb: Small and bright. You wake up to the shutters going up.

units.name: Flat above the shop
units.blurb: Two rooms over the family shop, with a shared courtyard behind.

units.name: Courtyard house
units.blurb: A whole little house on the lane. The family keeps it for people they like.

quirks.text: Rent includes a shift at the family stall during festival week. You can skip it and nobody will say anything, but everyone will remember.
The lanes are halfling-heavy, and by your second week everybody knows your name.

neighbors.name: Grandmother Adaeze Oduya-Venn
neighbors.who: Keeps the family books, and a list of who helped out in festival week.
neighbors.hook: Being on her good list opens doors all over the Market Ring.

neighbors.name: Tobin Venn
neighbors.who: The grandson.
neighbors.hook: He'd sell the whole block to Brightlane if anyone let him.

units.name: Studio
units.blurb: Clean, beige and approved. There's a smart meter by the door.

units.name: One-bed above the arcade
units.blurb: Arcade noise until late, but the hot water actually works.

units.name: Two-bed "premium"
units.blurb: The same as the one-bed, plus a second room and a logo on the door.

quirks.text: Complaints go to a form that sends you to another form.
Repairs do happen eventually, carried out by a contractor who won't speak to you.
Corporate-funded: anything you run from here is outside Commons protection.

neighbors.name: Linnea Sato
neighbors.who: A Crownline billing clerk. Very nice.
neighbors.hook: Reports everything she sees.

units.name: Room with a shared kitchen
units.blurb: A room of your own, a kitchen everyone shares, and a rota on the fridge.

units.name: Workshop flat
units.blurb: On the ground floor, with a workbench. Wrenches love it.

units.name: Family flat
units.blurb: Three rooms over the bakery.

quirks.text: Pay the full rent, or pay 20 less and put in a weekly repair shift.
The results of house votes arrive in your mail every second Thursday.

neighbors.name: Marisol Teague
neighbors.who: Chairs the Tenants' Table this month, and every month nobody else wants to.
neighbors.hook: Always short of hands for the boiler room.

neighbors.name: Kettle
neighbors.who: Fixes the boilers and keeps a tally of who helped.
neighbors.hook: Can tell you exactly who on the block owes the Table what.

units.name: Crew bunk
units.blurb: A bunk in a four-berth room for Meridian crew. Lockers lock, mostly.

units.name: Waterfront room
units.blurb: A room with a window over the water. The foghorn is included.

units.name: Harbor-view flat
units.blurb: Two rooms with a balcony over the cranes.

quirks.text: Lose your Meridian contract and the crew bunk reprices to the waterfront rate the next Monday.
Freight work starts at your door, so dock gigs are only a walk away.
Corporate-funded: anything you run from here is outside Commons protection.

neighbors.name: Sefa Morrow
neighbors.who: A crane operator, quietly organizing the crew.
neighbors.hook: Needs someone to carry messages that Meridian can't read.

units.name: A corner of a shared roof
units.blurb: Under a tarp, among friends. Probably.

units.name: A built-on room
units.blurb: Somebody's extension of somebody else's extension.

quirks.text: The registry doesn't recognize these addresses, so anything that needs a formal address is Hard.
Tangle Clan routes go everywhere, if you know who to ask.

neighbors.name: Skrit
neighbors.who: Holds the roof stack by Lantern Steps.
neighbors.hook: Will trade a bed for a fixed relay.

quirks.text: Staff positions sometimes come with a room. You ask the household for one, not the PDA.
The terraced gardens are older than the city wall, and the gardeners live on the grounds.
During court season, visiting delegations are put up here. Everyone else is shown the gate.
The household hasn't let a room in living memory, and fae memory is long.

units.name: Servants' wing room
units.blurb: Old, quiet and well kept. Meals are served whether you want them or not.

units.name: Carriage house
units.blurb: Your own door, your own stairs, and a family across the gravel watching both.

quirks.text: Invitations come through Standing, not money.
An address on the Row opens doors that credits alone don't.

neighbors.name: Lady Corvina Marsh
neighbors.who: The head of the house with the carriage house.
neighbors.hook: Collects tenants the way other people collect stories.

units.name: Scholar's room
units.blurb: The rate for enrolled students and staff. Your paperwork has to be current.

units.name: Visiting room
units.blurb: The same room at the rate for anyone not enrolled.

quirks.text: Let a term lapse and the room reprices, and you get a form explaining why.
The kitchens are shared, so someone is always cooking.

neighbors.name: Professor Ilse Vantongeren
neighbors.who: On her ninth "temporary" room in the Dells.
neighbors.hook: Pays well for research help. Doesn't ask where it came from.

units.name: Shared room
units.blurb: Two beds, two desks and one window that doesn't open. The enrolled rate.

units.name: Single room
units.blurb: A door that locks, and a desk that's actually yours.

quirks.text: Mixed peoples and mixed disciplines mean somebody down the hall knows the thing you need.
The walls are thin and exam season is loud.

neighbors.name: Quill
neighbors.who: A second-year who runs a tutoring business.
neighbors.hook: Also runs a better one, in exam answers.

units.name: Holdout flat
units.blurb: The old rent. It stays this low for as long as you pay, or until the next "improvement".

units.name: Renovated unit
units.blurb: Glass, steel, a smart lock, and a view of the holdouts.

quirks.text: A buyout letter arrives every month.
The court is half old homes and half glass, and the two halves don't talk.
Corporate-funded: anything you run from here is outside Commons protection.

neighbors.name: The Halloran sisters
neighbors.who: Have lived on the ground floor since before Glassline arrived.
neighbors.hook: They won't sell, and they could use help proving the court's old lease is still valid.

units.name: A bed, if admitted
units.blurb: A clean bed in a quiet hall. The lantern stays lit all night.

units.name: Lantern room
units.blurb: A room of your own, with a window onto the spires.

quirks.text: Nobody explains how admission is decided.
A kitchen or laundry shift takes 20 off the rent.

neighbors.name: Brother Ossel
neighbors.who: A keeper who counts the beds twice a night.
neighbors.hook: Notices when anyone's missing, and goes looking for them.

quirks.text: The keepers live here. Visitors are walked through, never put up.

units.name: Garden room
units.blurb: Opens onto a garden that someone's great-great-grandmother planted, and you will be reminded of it.

units.name: Altered house
units.blurb: Each generation added a room. None of them added a straight wall.

quirks.text: The renewal terms are written in a dialect that keeps changing.
The rent is fair and hasn't changed in a century. Literally.

neighbors.name: Thessaly Moor
neighbors.who: Reads the lease aloud on the first of every month to anyone who asks.
neighbors.hook: Is the only person who knows what clause nine actually says.

units.name: Shift bunk
units.blurb: Rented by the shift. Whoever gets there first keeps the blanket.

units.name: Crew room
units.blurb: A room shared with your shift.

units.name: Room with a lock that works
units.blurb: Rarer than it should be.

quirks.text: The bunks are double-booked more often than not.
Shipyard gigs start at your door.

neighbors.name: Jory Kell
neighbors.who: A rivet foreman who has slept in Bunk 9 for eleven years.
neighbors.hook: He'll tell you about it, and about who keeps taking Bunk 9.

units.name: A swept-out room
units.blurb: Former service rooms with no windows, as quiet as a held breath.

quirks.text: No windows, no registry entry and no mail delivery.
Nobody official is looking for you down here.

neighbors.name: Nan Gutter
neighbors.who: Keeps the lamps lit and the way in quiet.
neighbors.hook: Wants to know who's been leaving chalk marks.

units.name: A cot in the pocket
units.blurb: Among people who dig, sort and share.

quirks.text: Ask before you enter. Stay by being useful.

neighbors.name: Mossback
neighbors.who: Digs deeper than anyone should.
neighbors.hook: Has found something down there they won't describe.

units.name: A room on the row
units.blurb: Where people actually live down here: patched, lit and claimed.
units.pay: keeping quiet about the way in

quirks.text: The neighbors watch out for you, because down here everyone has to.

neighbors.name: Garrow Fenn
neighbors.who: Keeps the row's water filter running.
neighbors.hook: Needs parts from the surface and can't go up for them.

units.name: Room under a shared roof
units.blurb: Dry most nights, thanks to the neighbors.

units.name: Two rooms and a patched skylight
units.blurb: Plenty of light, and a bucket for when it rains.

quirks.text: Miss rent and you're asked onto the roof crew, not shown the door.
A weekly roof repair takes 20 off the rent.

neighbors.name: Ama Kwarteng
neighbors.who: The roof crew boss.
neighbors.hook: Can tell a leak from three floors down, and will tell you about yours.

units.name: Landing room
units.blurb: Right on the landing, next to the rail everyone mends.

units.name: Stair-top flat
units.blurb: The top of the stair, with the best view and the most steps.

quirks.text: Keep the landing swept and Auntie Pell forgets the odd late week.
Auntie Pell has opinions about the stair, the landing, and you.

neighbors.name: Wick
neighbors.who: Sweeps the landing twice so you don't have to, for a price.
neighbors.hook: Saves up for something they won't name.

units.name: Room over the noodle shop
units.blurb: Warm and loud, and it smells great at lunch.

units.name: Room over the repair stall
units.blurb: Soldering fumes from eight until six.

units.name: Corner room, two windows
units.blurb: The best room on the block, priced like it.

quirks.text: Rent goes up whenever the shop below has a bad week.
Repairs are "on the list".

neighbors.name: Lio Banerjee
neighbors.who: Has a list of every "on the list" repair since 2019.
neighbors.hook: Wants help taking it to Public Advocacy.

units.name: Crew room, if there's space
units.blurb: Patchkin crews get first pick. You get what's left.

units.name: Row house
units.blurb: Built from whatever the fields gave up. It's sturdier than it looks.

quirks.text: A sorting shift in the yards takes 20 off the rent.
A good find pays rent better than credits do.

neighbors.name: Nettle
neighbors.who: A Patchkin crew boss.
neighbors.hook: Judges everyone by what they bring back.

units.name: Tent space
units.blurb: Ground, a windbreak, and a fire someone else lit.
units.pay: news, water or a hand with the stakes

quirks.text: Ask first. The Dustwalkers remember who was kind.

neighbors.name: Old Tamsin
neighbors.who: Keeps the camp's story book.
neighbors.hook: Pays in water for any story she hasn't heard.

units.name: Floor by the stove
units.blurb: Warm, crowded and honest.

units.name: A room for regulars
units.blurb: Earned by coming back.

quirks.text: Regulars get the rooms. Everyone else gets the floor by the stove.
The last beds before open country, so you're the first to hear road news.

neighbors.name: Corran Dask
neighbors.who: A long-haul driver who's stopped here every month for twenty years.
neighbors.hook: Knows which roads Bastion watches.

units.name: Crew room
units.blurb: Rented to Riverbend crews at the crew rate.

units.name: Room
units.blurb: The same room at the rate for anyone not on the crew.

quirks.text: Miss a shift and it shows up on your rent.
Corporate-funded: anything you run from here is outside Commons protection.

neighbors.name: Hedda Stonebrook
neighbors.who: A union steward in all but name.
neighbors.hook: Wants proof of the shift-docking before the Labor Board will listen.

units.name: Room on the row
units.blurb: Your roof gets kept on, and so does everyone else's.

units.name: House with a workshop
units.blurb: There's a bench out back and a door wide enough for a cart.

quirks.text: Rent goes into the shared repair tin, and the tin gets counted in public.
A repair shift on the row takes 20 off the rent.

neighbors.name: Saint Rusty
neighbors.who: Keeps the tin.
neighbors.hook: Has never once miscounted it, and wants that on the record.

units.name: Chamber bunk
units.blurb: A bunk in a shared chamber, dry most of the year.

units.name: Dry room
units.blurb: A chamber of your own with a curtain for a door.

units.name: Family chamber
units.blurb: Two chambers knocked through, with a vent that actually draws.

quirks.text: Radio Sewers is down the walkway, so warnings reach you first.
In flood weeks the pumps fail and everyone sleeps on the upper walkways.
If the rats are nervous, so is the whole stack.
A pump-watch shift takes 15 off the rent.

neighbors.name: Mother Gutterlight
neighbors.who: Keeps the pump log and decides who gets a chamber.
neighbors.hook: Wants someone to find out who keeps opening the lower sluice.

neighbors.name: Tally
neighbors.who: A courier who lives on the walkway and knows every pipe gate.
neighbors.hook: Will run anything anywhere, as long as it isn't through Pipe 37.

units.name: Bunk by the desk
units.blurb: First to hear when a job comes in. Last to get any sleep.

units.name: Room with a lock
units.blurb: A door, a lock and a window onto the Walk.

units.name: Back room, two exits
units.blurb: For people who like having options.

quirks.text: Fixers check the Callback's desk first, so gigs find you here.
Take one of Vane's jobs a week and she knocks 10 off the rent.
Everyone at the Callback is waiting for work, and some of them want yours.
Leave by the back exit and Vane will know which job you took.

neighbors.name: Hollis Crane
neighbors.who: Ex-Bastion. Has been waiting on a job for three months and pretending he isn't.
neighbors.hook: Knows how Bastion runs a recovery, and might tell you for a drink.

neighbors.name: Fizzwick
neighbors.who: Paints names on the waiting board.
neighbors.hook: Moves names up the board for a fee.

units.name: Room over the parts store
units.blurb: Cheap, and you'll know every delivery by its engine.

units.name: Two-room walk-up
units.blurb: A kitchen, a bedroom and a window onto Coil Lane.

units.name: Top flat with a roof bench
units.blurb: There's a workbench on the roof. On a clear night, the best view on the Row.

quirks.text: Shops below, homes above: you'll hear the work start at six.
A shift at Third Rattle Motors takes 20 off the rent.
It smells like oil, and your clothes will too.

neighbors.name: Bolt Rattle
neighbors.who: Granny's grandson, and the best diagnostician on the Row.
neighbors.hook: Wants to open his own shop, without breaking Granny's heart.

neighbors.name: Agnes Fenwick
neighbors.who: A retired welder.
neighbors.hook: Keeps a spare torch for anyone who asks nicely.

units.name: Studio over the square
units.blurb: Polished floors, a view of the trams, and a concierge who knows your name.

units.name: One-bed with a tram view
units.blurb: A bedroom away from the bells.

units.name: Clock-face suite
units.blurb: Behind the clock itself. The light comes through the numerals.

quirks.text: It's two minutes to Transfer Square and every tram line.
The concierge logs every visitor, and the log isn't private.
Corporate-funded: anything you run from here is outside Commons protection.

neighbors.name: Delphine Okafor-Reyes
neighbors.who: A Velvet Signal producer.
neighbors.hook: Always looking for a story, and for someone to be in it.

neighbors.name: Mister Quell
neighbors.who: Has lived in the clock-face suite for sixty years, under four managements.
neighbors.hook: Knows which floors the managers never visit.

units.name: Bunk on a working barge
units.blurb: Cargo by day and your bed by night. Mind the hatch.

units.name: Cabin on a houseboat
units.blurb: A little stove, a round window and the river right outside.

units.name: A whole narrowboat
units.blurb: Yours from bow to stern, as long as it floats.

quirks.text: Once a season the boats move berths, and your address moves with them.
Flood weeks rock the boats, so don't keep anything fragile.
A boat ride beats the roads, if you know the water routes.

neighbors.name: Dorrit Wennick
neighbors.who: The captain's sister. Sells smoked fish off the stern.
neighbors.hook: Hears every rumor that comes down the river.

neighbors.name: Silt
neighbors.who: Lives under the moorings.
neighbors.hook: Knows what's in the water, and who put it there.

units.name: Emergency bed
units.blurb: A real address, a locker and a waitlist number.

quirks.text: A real address, a waitlist and a bad mood.
The Advocates Steps are across the square, if you need help with an eviction from Public Advocacy.
You don't rent a room here. You're placed in one when you've lost your home.

neighbors.name: Clerk Imogen Pask
neighbors.who: Assigns the beds.
neighbors.hook: Remembers who said thank you, and moves them up the list.

units.name: Contractor bunk
units.blurb: Contract rate for anyone working a Crownline contract.

units.name: Dorm room
units.blurb: The same room at the rate for anyone not on a contract.

units.name: Supervisor's room
units.blurb: A door, a desk, and a window that faces away from the stacks.

quirks.text: Lights out on the shift whistle, whether your shift is over or not.
The Overtime Canteen is next door.
Corporate-funded: anything you run from here is outside Commons protection.

neighbors.name: Rook Tallis
neighbors.who: Says he's just a pipe fitter.
neighbors.hook: Has Bastion boots under his bunk.
